newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta index ends lower on big-cap selling.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta index ends lower on big-cap selling.

text.p: Jakarta share prices ended lower on Friday due to continued selling in several big-capitalised stocks led by cigarette maker Sampoerna, brokers said.

But they said buying interest remained strong in several counters which were subject to rumours ranging from being the possible target of take-overs to the announcement of bonus-share and rights issues.
The Jakarta Composite Index closed down 4.55 points, or 0.64 percent, at 705.37 points after an earlier low of 702.32 points. Losers lead gainers by 70 to 54, with 59 counters unchanged.
Total turnover was 533.7 billion rupiah on a volume of 200.6 million shares.
"Some counters are considered expensive. Technically, there should be some correction" he added.
Brokers said the market was likely to move in the narrow-range on Monday with more interest in secondaries likely to be driven by local speculative buying.

Blue-chip Sampoerna, which has a weight of 5.65 percent on the composite index, tumbled 10.53 percent to close at 11,900 rupiah on a volume about six million shares after plunging to 11,600 rupiah earlier.
Brokers said it was due to continued selling by overseas investors following its lower-than-expected 1996 net profit announced on Thursday.
Shares price of Gudang Garam, Sampoerna's main competitor, also subsided due to profit taking. It fell 200 rupiah to 11,675 rupiah on 175,500 shares.
Stocks which fell on profit taking included telecommunications firm Indosat, cement maker Semen Gresik and tin miner Tambang Timah, brokers said.
Third-liner property company Elang Realty was the most active stock on what brokers said due to intense market talk that the firm had been targeted for a take-over by local conglomerates.
It rose 100 rupiah to 975 on 26.6 million shares.
